items.title: 53571_Mary Lou Williams oral history interview
items.q: Mr. Orion that owned this place liked me also because he was crazy about Garland.

ctx.x: Then when you got to Paris, how did this develop?

I worked there for a while, for about I guess a month. Garland Wilson was there and he passed away, he died, you know. It's a place where the customers that really frequent this place didn't like women, but I got in because I was a friend of his. Mr. Orion that owned this place liked me also because he was crazy about Garland. So I got a job there for about 2 months. I was doubling at the theatre, making money. All the Americans had gone back to America and they had so many things for you to do because they had…

my salary and that's the worst thing you can do in Paris because you'll never get it. But I ran into a wonderful drummer, Gerard Pochonet. He used to play for all the Americans when they came over. He was on a newspaper and everything so he got my money and everything else, you know, for me. He took me out to his house in the country to stay with he and his grandmother.
